mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of quarters where GDPC1 growth is positive (quarterly YoY growth > 0.5%) over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate below 0.25% signals an aggressive monetary easing policy, which reduces risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.25% occurs in at least 30% of 5-day return windows, but the average 5-day return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) compared to the market baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust economic growth across manufacturing and construction sectors, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between INDPRO and HOUST (measured as correlation > 0.7 over 3 months) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 8.0%), a decline in the unemployment rate signals improving labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 8.0%, the average 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) compared to the market baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in a recovery phase.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL shows a monthly increase in more than 60% of 60-day return windows, but the average 60-day return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) compared to the market baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 650.0 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: HOUST < 650.0 occurs in at least 30% of 5-day return windows, but the average 5-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) compared to the market baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in housing starts (HOUST) and residential sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand in the housing sector, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between HOUST and RSAFS (measured as correlation > 0.7 over 3 months) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 220.0), a decline in the consumer price index signals a potential easing of inflationary pressures, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates a reduction in monetary policy tightening.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 220.0, a decline in CPIAUCSL leads to negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances over the last 10 years.
